A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same integer-programming causal-bootstrap work and retain matching simulation settings and theoretical material. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison despite retitling and substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original geographical-experiment simulations using IMF GDP data, including coverage, confidence-interval widths, and power in Tables 1–4.

after.justification: v2 retains the original GDP simulation results and adds measured runtime scaling results in Section 5 and Appendix 7.8.

M1.justification: The variance-maximizing integer program, marginal constraints and slackness relaxation, estimator extensions, and rerandomization bootstrap are retained. The bounded-confounding theorem extends the analysis. The newly disclosed faster LP implementation does not establish a revision to the proposed statistical procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate country-GDP simulations with null, additive, and multiplicative effects under complete randomization and matched pairs, with and without covariate adjustment. The new runtime sweep varies sample size within retained designs; the four-unit appendix example is an analytical construction.

E2.justification: v2 removes the remaining isotone-copula comparisons for matched-pairs injected-effect experiments from Tables 2–4. That baseline remains in the A/A comparison in Table 1 and in complete-randomization comparisons. Sampling bootstrap and conservative variance baselines are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix 7.8 adds a runtime evaluation under a null effect while varying the number of units, using integer programming for matched pairs and linear programming for complete randomization. The original accuracy experiments retain their data selection, assignments, estimators, and resampling budgets.

E4.justification: v2 adds a computational scalability analysis examining runtime versus sample size and a four-unit undercoverage case analysis in Appendix 7.11. The existing covariate, assignment-design, and injected-effect comparisons were already present in v1.

E5.justification: The new runtime plots report averages over 10 simulation runs with 95% confidence intervals based on standard errors. This adds uncertainty reporting for runtime measurements; the original bootstrap and coverage reporting practices remain unchanged.

E6.justification: All retained numerical entries in Tables 1–4 match. v2 removes relative-width percentages and matched-pairs isotone results, including Table 2's covariate-adjusted width/power values 66/0.69 and 193/1.00. It adds mean runtimes at 50 units: 671 seconds for matched-pairs IP, 1057 for complete-randomization IP, and 22 for complete-randomization LP.

T1.justification: v2 adds bounded-confounding assumptions, Theorems 2/4, Lemma 2, and an extended proof in Appendix 7.5, plus the four-unit undercoverage construction. It also adds DKW-to-PMF reasoning and corrects a control-weight term in the earlier proof. Corollary 1 restates v1's Remark 1. The new confounding proof contains probability and slackness inconsistencies.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion replace broad applicability wording for any known probabilistic assignment with explicit validity claims for unconfounded, conditionally unconfounded, and individualistic bounded-confounding assignments. The bounded-confounding guarantee becomes a headline contribution, while general confounded validity remains open. The linear/quadratic estimator scope was already present.

C2.justification: v2 expands the existing undercoverage discussion with an example explicitly addressing its own method. Section 4.2 distinguishes program solvability from validity and identifies missing-outcome support restrictions as a possible failure condition. The runtime discussion additionally attributes faster matched-pairs optimization to covariance sparsity.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents using a faster LP implementation for complete randomization and supplies formulation-specific timings. The CP-SAT reference, 100-worker cluster, and approximately two-hour experiment runtime are retained. Conversely, v1's explicit pre-period growth-regression example in Section 4.1 is removed.

R1.justification: v2 adds Tan (2006) and De Bartolomeis et al. (2024) for bounded confounding and removes Sävje (2021). Related work more explicitly distinguishes the approach from Ji et al.'s dual optimal-transport framework and Harshaw et al.'s quadratic variance bounds.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled and Sections 2–4 are substantially reorganized around the core program, estimator generalizations, and assignment mechanisms. Confidence-interval construction moves to the appendix. The introduction, background, and experimental narrative are extensively restructured, including new Dataset, Settings, Baselines, Scalability, and Analysis paragraph headings.

P2.justification: v2 adds two runtime plots and small tables for the undercoverage example, removes percentage columns from Tables 2–4, expands design labels and captions, and relocates Algorithm 1 to Appendix 7.10. The overall single-column layout and existing result-table organization remain similar.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful runtime evidence, clearer organization, and more qualified applicability claims. However, its principal new confounding guarantee is internally inconsistent: Theorems 2/4's printed probability lower bound equals 16 at the permitted choice ε = δ, and Appendix 7.5's slackness substitution makes Equation 16's right-hand side 2ε rather than ε. These defects undermine a headline theoretical addition. The PDFs do not establish whether the documentation and presentation gains outweigh the added reliability problems.
